pharm: Topical demulcent; hydrophilic cellulose-derivative polymer that forms a viscous, water-retaining film to lubricate and stabilize the tear film.
quick: Instill 1-2 drops into affected eye(s) as needed
Eye pain, vision change, persistent redness
summary: Carboxymethylcellulose sodium ophthalmic solution is an over-the-counter artificial tear/ocular lubricant (commonly 0.5% or 1%) for the temporary relief of burning, irritation, and discomfort due to dryness of the eye. The cellulose polymer forms a lubricating, water-retaining film that stabilizes the tear film. It is for use in the eyes only and acts locally with negligible systemic absorption.
indications: Temporary relief of burning and irritation due to dryness of the eye
Temporary relief of discomfort due to minor eye irritation or exposure to wind and sun
Lubricant to prevent further irritation or to relieve dryness of the eye

dosage.d: Instill 1 or 2 drops into the affected eye(s)
dosage.n: For single-use containers: discard after use; do not reuse

admin: For use in the eyes only
To open a single-use vial, twist the tab completely off
Do not touch the tip of the container to any surface to avoid contamination
Instill 1-2 drops into the affected eye(s) as needed
Do not reuse single-use containers; discard once opened
Do not use if the solution changes color or becomes cloudy
moa: Carboxymethylcellulose sodium is a hydrophilic cellulose polymer that acts as a demulcent. On instillation it forms a viscous, water-retaining film over the ocular surface, lubricating the eye, increasing tear film stability and retention time, and protecting against further dryness and irritation. Its effect is purely local and physical, with no significant pharmacologic systemic activity.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to carboxymethylcellulose or any component of the product
relative: Do not use if solution changes color or becomes cloudy
monitor: Eye pain, changes in vision, continued redness or irritation
Symptoms that worsen or persist for more than 72 hours

preg: No relevant systemic exposure expected from topical ocular use; generally considered safe in pregnancy.
lact: No relevant systemic exposure expected from topical ocular use; generally considered safe during breastfeeding.
renal: No dose adjustment; minimal systemic absorption with topical ocular use.
hepatic: No dose adjustment; minimal systemic absorption with topical ocular use.

serious: Worsening or persistent redness, pain, or vision change (stop use and seek care)

monitoring: Watch for eye pain, changes in vision, or continued redness/irritation
Reassess if the condition worsens or persists for more than 72 hours
counsel: For use in the eyes only
Instill 1-2 drops in the affected eye(s) as needed
Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface to avoid contamination
Discard single-use vials after use and do not reuse
Do not use if the solution changes color or becomes cloudy
Stop use and ask a doctor if you have eye pain, vision changes, or redness/irritation lasting more than 72 hours
Temporary blurring after instillation is normal; wait before driving or operating machinery
Keep out of reach of children; if swallowed, contact a Poison Control Center
pk: Not applicable; acts locally on the ocular surface
Store at room temperature; do not use if cloudy or discolored
pearls: OTC artificial tear; commonly available as 0.5% and 1% solutions
Acts as a physical lubricant/demulcent, not a pharmacologic agent
Preservative-free single-use vials are useful for frequent dosing or sensitive eyes
Persistent symptoms beyond 72 hours warrant evaluation for underlying eye disease
missed: Not applicable; used as needed for symptom relief. Instill a drop whenever dryness or irritation occurs.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with topical ocular use. Excess drops can be wiped away. If accidentally swallowed, contact a Poison Control Center; manage supportively.
